news.title: Elon Musk’s First Wife Speaks Out on His ‘Suicidal’ Mindset
news.text:
Elon Musk’s first wife is speaking out about his “apocalyptic” mentality.

Justine Musk, who was married to Musk from 2000 to 2008 and has six kids with him, told podcaster Kara Swisher that “everything is life and death” for her ex-husband. “I once described him as somebody who can jump off the edge of a cliff and invent a parachute on the way down,” she said. “I think he thrives on chaos.”

“If you listen to the language that he uses—and even taking into account that a lot of it is pitch; it’s performative—everything is very, very urgent,” Justine added. “‘We’re going to die.’ ‘The world is going to be destroyed.’” 

Swisher, an expert on all things Musk, declared the predisposition “almost suicidal, apocalyptic.” Justine agreed. 

“He really lives with that pitch of intensity, and that’s the place where he feels comfortable,” Justine said. “And so if he’s too comfortable, he looks for that chaos, and he brings it with him, and he has a way of, of sucking you into it. At first, it can look a lot like excitement. It’s that intensity. I think he really needs that.” 

The “method” behind the tech tycoon’s “madness” took center stage after he became Donald Trump’s right-hand, funneling nearly $300 million into his 2024 campaign.

Justine warned the public not to underestimate her ex. “I always assume that there’s a method to his madness,” she said, adding that he does “A lot of sleight of hand; ‘Look over here.’ And then he is doing something” out of view.

The upcoming documentary Musk, from filmmaker Alex Gibney—also a guest on the podcast—alleges that Musk used nefarious means to swing the election toward Trump. Gibney revealed to Swisher and Justine Musk the moment he became afraid Musk would retaliate for the scathing film. 

“I was foolishly not scared at the beginning because it felt like a continuation of a lot of the stuff that I had done,” he said. “I had done an investigation in the Church of Scientology, the Roman Catholic Church, the guys at Enron, the U.S. government. So foolishly, I just thought, well, I’ll just do my thing” when it comes to Musk.

“It didn’t occur to me, once Elon Musk essentially became the shadow president or had this weird symbiotic relationship with Donald Trump, suddenly, that was a different kind of power,” Gibney added. “And you realize that even the rule of law was not gonna save you.”

Musk has repeatedly attacked Gibney and his credibility, melting down about the films’ accusations on X. The Tesla CEO called the documentary “a hit piece.”

Added Swisher on her own “concerns” about retaliation, “One thing someone told me, ‘cause I’ve been pretty hostile to a lot of tech people, is, ‘How can you do it?’ I said, ‘Well, they’re gonna have to shoot me in front of everybody. That’s what’s gonna have to happen here. So people can see. And that’s one thing or another. It’s not gonna be quiet.” 

As for the former Mrs. Musk, Swisher said she sympathized with her more “personal” connection to Elon because of their shared children. 

“This is like the ex from hell,” Swisher said.

news.title: World News | Trump Dismisses Reports of Potential Strikes on Iran, Says “productive Discussions” Ongoing, No Attacks Before Midterms
news.text:
Washington DC [US], October 8 (ANI): US President Donald Trump on Thursday dismissed reports of possible fresh strikes against Iran, saying “productive discussions” are underway with Tehran and making clear that the United States will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the blockade on Iranian maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place while claiming that oil was continuing to flow in record volumes through the strategic waterways with no Iranian oil involved. 

Also Read | Freddie Jackson Death: Grammy-Nominated R&B Singer, Known for 'You Are My Lady', Dies at 69; Family Pays Tribute.

He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to possess a nuclear weapon.

“We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran. I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect, with Oil flowing in Record Numbers of Barrels through the Hormuz Strait (22 Million Barrels, last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran!), we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd. IRAN WILL NOT HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON!” the post read.

Also Read | Indian IT Giants Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Suspended From US PERM Programme: What It Means For Green Card Applicants.

Trump's statement came a day after reports that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran, potentially ahead of the midterms.

Axios report that Trump had not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations against Iran, but that the Pentagon had been instructed to prepare for possible fresh strikes.

According to Axios, citing US officials, the Pentagon instructed US Central Command several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran. The directive did not set a specific date for any potential strikes.

US and Israeli officials cited by the publication said renewed combat operations could take place before the US midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, and possibly ahead of Israeli elections expected a week earlier.

However, Trump's latest statement ruled out an attack before the US midterm elections while saying that discussions with Iran were continuing.

Meanwhile, earlier in the day, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran would respond to a US peace proposal within the next few days, noting that the negotiations between Tehran and Washington remained ongoing and that messages were continuing to be exchanged through mediators.

“The negotiation process is still ongoing and messages are being exchanged through mediators,” Araghchi said, as quoted by Iranian state media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB).

The Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran had already presented its proposal, referred to as the “Seven-Day Plan”, and had received the US side's views on it.

“We presented our plan, which we had presented under the title 'Seven-Day Plan', and we also heard the American side's views on it,” Araghchi said.

“We are currently reviewing the views of the Americans and I think we will provide our response within the next few days,” he added.

The ongoing diplomatic exchanges are linked to Tehran's proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz under a seven-day plan, which Araghchi presented last month during the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Araghchi had said the timeline for the proposal would begin once the United States accepted it.

According to Al Jazeera, he said Washington would need to take certain actions under the plan, which could be completed within four to five days.

“If they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow,” Araghchi said.

He said the required steps were already part of a memorandum of understanding and would not be difficult to implement. Under the proposal, if the US fulfilled the conditions, the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened on the sixth day, followed by renewed talks between Tehran and Washington on the seventh day.

Trump had earlier rejected the proposed arrangement, according to The Wall Street Journal. (ANI)

Man accused of murdering three family members 'not sorry' for father or brother but sorry for mother

When asked why he had killed three members of his family, counsel said that Robert O’Connor told gardaí he had a row over drugs, only meant to kill his father and brother but not his mother and had “lost my head”.

7.15pm, 8 Oct 2026

Share options

A 32-YEAR-OLD MAN who is accused of murdering three members of his family at their Co Louth home last year told gardaí that he had stabbed his younger special needs brother like a “blood bag”, a Central Criminal Court jury has heard.

The jurors were also told they will hear evidence that the three victims sustained a combined 139 stab wounds.

Roisin Lacey SC, for the Director of Public Prosecutions, said in her opening speech today that the accused Robert O’Connor told gardaí that he had a row over drugs, lost his head and only meant to kill his father and brother, but not his mother.

When re-arraigned before the Central Criminal Court this afternoon, Robert O’Connor, of Drumgowna, Louth Village, Dundalk, Co Louth, pleaded not guilty of murder by reason of insanity or guilty of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility to the triple murder of his mother Louise O’Connor (56), his father Mark O’Connor (54) and his younger brother Evan O’Connor (27) at their home in Drumgowna between 28 and 29 September 2025, both dates inclusive.

Opening the prosecution’s case, Lacey said the accused Robert O’Connor accepts he caused the death of the three victims in the case.

Counsel said the deaths of the three victims occurred sometime between Sunday 28 September and Monday 29 September but that the actual times of their deaths were not entirely clear.

Referring to the accused man’s younger brother Evan O’Connor, Lacey said he had very significant special needs, was severely autistic and had learning difficulties. She said Evan was supported by a charitable organisation, who provided learning and living support.

Counsel said a carer had arrived at Drumgowna at 9.30am on the morning of 29 September. “Just before the carer reversed in on the Monday, she saw something and thought it looked like a Halloween decoration of some kind inside the gate,” said the barrister.

The lawyer said the carer waited for Evan and when he didn’t come out, she thought this was unusual. She said the carer got out of the car and walked back towards the gate, where she saw the “heavily blood-stained body” of Mark O’Connor inside the front gate of the house.

When the carer looked across at the house, she saw Evan’s body lying across the step of the patio door with blood on the bottom of his legs.

Lacey said the jury will hear that the carer got back into the car and drove to a neighbour’s house, where she called 999 at 9.38am that morning. Gardaí and members of the armed support unit arrived at Drumgowna later that morning.

Lacey said the evidence will be that beside Mark O’Connor’s body was a beer bottle, an orange kitchen knife and a butter knife.

The lawyer told the jurors that when gardaí entered the house sometime later, they observed Louise O’Connor’s body “equally heavily bloodstained” on the kitchen floor.

She said a local doctor arrived sometime later and pronounced each of the three victims dead.

The court will also hear evidence, the lawyer said, that gardaí took statements from various individuals who had heard something the night before, or had encountered the accused man on the morning of 29 September.

Counsel said the jury would hear evidence from a neighbour, who will say that he recognised the accused man’s voice coming from the O’Connor household on the night of 28 September saying: “I’ll end you, I’ll fu*king end you”.

Counsel told the panel that the same neighbour saw the accused man at his gate on the morning of 29 September. Lacey said the witness will say that Robert O’Connor was “agitated, which was not unusual” and that the accused told him: “I’m sorry about the noise last night, where do we go now?”

Another neighbour heard the accused man shouting and cursing around 8.30pm on the evening of 28 September.

There will be evidence from another neighbour, Lacey said, who described a strange noise like a “horse kind of noise” but recognised it as a male voice. Around 8.45pm on 28 September, the same neighbour saw a male figure in the middle of the back garden of Drumgowna, jumping up and down in the air.

The lawyer said this neighbour’s wife had sent a Facebook message to Louise O’Connor that evening asking her if everything was alright, but didn’t receive any response back.

The prosecution barrister went on to tell the court that a woman had gone to the front of her house around 9.45am on the morning of 29 September when she saw a shadow pass across her window. When the woman opened the door, Robert O’Connor was there and he apologised to her, saying he didn’t want to frighten her.

Lacey said the evidence will be that the accused said: “I can’t put it into words, it’s all muddled in my head, they tortured me for years, my family, they manipulated me for years.”

Advertisement

Counsel said the accused asked could he come into her house as he wanted “to charge” but she refused. When the woman asked the accused what happened, Robert O’Connor said “I killed them”.

When the woman asked him whether the sirens were for him, the accused man said “yes”. Lacey said the woman found the accused level-headed and not aggressive in any way before he headed off in the direction of Tallanstown. The woman rang 999 at 10.04am that morning.

There will be evidence, Lacey said, that gardaí had observed the accused on foot walking in the direction of Tallanstown that morning. When they stopped the accused, he was highly aggressive and agitated and shouted at them: “I’m looking for ye”.

When gardaí asked the accused to show them his hands, he refused and shouted: “Shoot me, shoot me.” The accused’s hands were blood-stained at the time, the court heard.

Lacey said that when the accused was arrested on suspicion of killing his parents and brother, he told gardaí: “I killed them; I killed my mother, father and my brother.”

The accused man also told detectives: “I slashed my mother, she gave me a look and I could see a reflection of my dad in her face.”

Robert O’Connor said his father Mark was behind his mother and he had killed him next and then his brother.

When asked why he had killed three members of his family, counsel said that Robert O’Connor told gardaí he had a row over drugs, only meant to kill his father and brother but not his mother and had “lost my head”.

The accused man also told gardaí he had stabbed his brother Evan like a “blood bag”.

Lacey said when the accused was in the back of a garda car, he said he was “not sorry for his father or brother” but was sorry for stabbing his mother to death. The accused said he had stabbed his mother in the forehead in the sitting room following an argument.

The accused added: “I stabbed my father with a kitchen knife from a block of five knives. I left when I stabbed my father and mother. I went back for my brother and stabbed him. I stabbed him like a blood bag”.

Counsel said the jury would hear that the accused told gardaí he had been using cocaine lately and had bought some ‘Wildcat’; which counsel said is a slang word for mephedrone and is an amphetamine. She said it was a synthetic drug and the effect on the body was similar to cocaine.

Lacey said the evidence will be the accused told gardaí that his parents had wanted to speak to him about his drug consumption but Robert O’Connor had told them he did not want to stop taking cocaine.

The accused also told detectives in Drogheda Garda Station that he had gone upstairs to take cocaine and watch pornography on the evening of 28 September. When the accused went back downstairs, the three others were in the sitting room and Robert told gardaí he “went for a knife”.

The accused said he was angry and asked his mother why she did not feel empathy. He said he first slashed his mother on the head with a kitchen knife and made the three of them stand with their heads down. The accused said his mother ran for the door and that his father had started to charge to the door.

The defendant said he “stabbed them multiple times and accepted he had killed them”.

Counsel said the accused also told gardaí that the “algorithm on Evan’s iPad” was affecting his reality. “I kept asking him was he the programmer,” the accused said.

When interviewed by gardaí, the accused said he had a feeling some of the drugs he took earlier had affected him.

Robert O’Connor told gardaí he was running around the garden with a wheelbarrow full of water and had done pull-ups in the garden. He said he had taken the three deceased outside and “had to throw them out to see who got into heaven”.

Counsel said the accused also told gardaí he had used a knife and didn’t remember leaving it in a log cabin.

Counsel said the jury would hear that Mark O’Connor had 44 stab wounds, with nine of those to his head; that Louise O’Connor suffered 20 stab wounds, with eight to her trunk, while Evan O’Connor had 75 stab wounds, with 25 of those to his head and neck.

Counsel said a pathologist will say Evan was alive when the vast majority of his wounds were sustained.

Lacey will continue her opening speech on Friday before Judge Mícheál P O’Higgins and a jury of six men and six women. The trial is expected to last until 30 October.

news.title: Inside Trump investigation of Wells Fargo's Black homeownership program
news.text:
The Trump administration is investigating a Wells Fargo program to increase the homeownership rate of Black Americans, signaling a sharp escalation in its broadside against diversity, equity and inclusion programs.

The Department of Housing and Urban Development opened the federal civil rights probe, accusing the bank of sorting homeowners by race. 

Craig Trainor, assistant secretary for fair housing and equal opportunity, told bank CEO Charlie Scharf in a letter that the agency would scrutinize the bank’s commitment to expanding access to home loans for Black Americans and other minority groups. 

“Even if Wells Fargo did not violate the law, its practice of dividing Americans based on race is immoral, unethical and un-American,” HUD Secretary Scott Turner said in a statement. “Wells Fargo and all of its employees that engaged in race-based decision-making should be ashamed of themselves.”

Wells Fargo declined to comment. The bank has been hit in recent years by allegations it discriminates against Black customers. The bank faced backlash after a Bloomberg report found it rejected half of all refinancing applications from Black families in 2020. 

In the view of the Trump administration, these programs violate fair housing law and discriminate against other homebuyers. A senior HUD official told the Wall Street Journal the agency is reviewing similar initiatives at other financial institutions.

Fair housing advocates say the Wells Fargo program was created under federal rules that expressly allowed it.

"Congress wrote Special Purpose Credit Programs (SPCPs) into federal law 50 years ago to enable lenders to adopt programs to remedy the effects of historic barriers and exclusions from the lending market based on gender, race and national origin," Nikitra Bailey, executive vice president of the National Fair Housing Alliance, said in a statement.

"Investigating a bank for following the government's own rules to create paths to address longstanding discrimination in lending is an abuse of the agency’s investigative authority and a transparent attempt to scare every lender in the nation away from their legal obligation to serve underserved communities," she said.

Wells Fargo pledged $150 million to reduce mortgage rates and refinancing fees for qualifying Black homeowners. HUD accused Wells Fargo of dividing Americans by race in violation of the Fair Housing Act, a civil rights-era law prohibiting discrimination based on factors such as race. 

“Attempting to close statistical racial gaps in homeownership by doling out loans based on race is no way to do business,” Trainor wrote. “And doing so in residential real estate-related transactions is illegal under the Fair Housing Act.”

The investigation into mortgage lending practices to minority groups is a shot across the bow to financial institutions engaged in race-based lending practices that the Trump administration says proliferated during the Biden administration. 

The Justice Department has launched antifraud probes into federal contractors, targeting DEI programs created after the 2020 murder of George Floyd. Since President Donald Trump’s election in 2024, many companies have walked away from these programs.

The Wells Fargo investigation not only marks a new chapter in the federal crackdown on corporate DEI initiatives, it exposes financial institutions to high-stakes government scrutiny and growing regulatory and legal risks.

Past administrations pressed banks to develop programs to close racial homeownership gaps. In 2024, less than a quarter of Black households owned the home they lived in compared with nearly three quarters of White households, according to the Pew Research Center.

Critics argue the administration is ignoring the legacy of government-backed redlining and restrictive covenants that barred Black and minority Americans from building wealth through homeownership. What's more, discrimination continues to unfairly limit access to homeownership as the nation faces an affordable housing crisis, they say.

“The Trump administration now appears increasingly interested in dismantling policies designed to acknowledge those consequences while invoking the language of equality to justify doing it,” citizen journalist George Cummings wrote on his "What Did Donald Trump Do Today?" Substack.

news.title: Arrests, detentions of Canadians in U.S. up 60 per cent, Ottawa says
news.text:
The number of arrest and detention cases involving Canadians citizens has jumped 60 per cent, Global Affairs Canada says.

The department’s annual report on consular cases, published Thursday, tracks an increase in arrests between April 2025 and March 2026, despite a 25 per cent decline in visits by Canadians to the U.S.

The report does not explain what caused the increase, though U.S. President Donald Trump has expanded immigration raids and Canadians have reported facing uncomfortable questions from U.S. border officials.

Overall, the report tracks a one-fifth increase in the number of arrests of Canadians around the world, including a threefold increase in the number of arrests in Thailand.

Global Affairs Canada has warned in recent years that the growing frequency of wars and natural disasters is resulting in more consular cases that are more complex and expensive to manage.

The data also shows an increase in the number of Canadians voluntarily registering with the department when they go abroad, which helps Ottawa send safety advice and co-ordinate evacuations.

news.title: Aerial Photos Show Reflecting Pool Work Progress As Trump Announces Refill
news.text: Aerial photos show different stages of the renovation work on the Reflecting Pool after U.S. President Donald Trump said the second round of renovations at the Lincoln Memorial site in Washington, D.C., was complete. “I think they’re going to fill it up this week. The Reflecting Pool is totally complete, and we changed the old pipes,” Trump told reporters. But the pool has not been filled as of Thursday morning, Newsweek's Leonardo Feldmen reported from the scene. Workers were still completing tasks on Wednesday, according to The Washington Post, seen spraying material on sections of the pool’s interior while grates for its center drain were not yet in place. Newsweek contacted the White House and the U.S. Department of the Interior, via email, for comment. What Aerial Photos Show Photos from the Washington Monument webcam overlooking the Memorial Reflecting Pool show water still visible on July 11, before the pool was drained for the second time. Crews began draining 4 million gallons of water in July, after major controversy over the $14 million no-bid contract, including severe algae outbreaks, peeling underwater coating and allegations of vandalism. The project had been declared complete in time for the nation’s 250th anniversary, but these issues developed within days. The Trump administration blamed political opponents and vandals for the project's rapid deterioration, but critics have questioned whether the claims were being used to mask systemic construction defects. Newsweek has broken down a timeline of the project, in detail, here. Pictures from July 14 show the pool without any water in it, exposing its basin and visible surface patterns. Images from Wednesday, a day after Trump said the work was complete, show the pool still drained but with changes in the surface visible. Close-up photos taken by Newsweek show the exposed basin with construction equipment scattered across the surface. What To Know About The Vandalism Case In June, the Trump administration alleged vandalism, saying law enforcement had found “deliberate slashes cut through the liner, sides, and coating, as well as fencing and debris thrown into the pool.” Olympic canoeist David Hearn was one of several people arrested before he was later indicted for felony destruction of property, but federal prosecutors dropped the criminal case after concluding that damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool was caused by flawed installation rather than vandalism. Last week, Judge Todd Edelman permanently dismissed the criminal case against Hearn, saying: "Within a month, the government recognized that its prosecution lacked merit. It reached this conclusion not because it had misidentified Mr. Hearn as the perpetrator of the alleged act, but because no crime had occurred." When reached for comment, the White House referred Newsweek to a series of Truth Social posts from President Donald Trump in August in which he blamed vandals for the damage to the reflecting pool. "Look what VANDALS did to the grass connecting the vandalized World War II Monument and the vandalized Reflecting Pool, which will be opened again, and better than ever, shortly," Trump wrote at the time. "Anybody who thinks the Reflecting Pool wasn’t vandalized should go back to Law School! The grass is being replaced shortly, and the Reflecting Pool is almost completely fixed, including the various inflow and outflow pipes, which we were saving for the end of the year, but will do now." Hearn's attorneys have since called for a "detailed and comprehensive" investigation into the prosecution of Hearn. "The Department of Justice and the Department of the Interior subjected an innocent man to a nightmare of wrongful arrest, felony indictment, and public defamation to cover up their own botched, rushed renovation of the Reflecting Pool," Hearn's attorneys previously told Newsweek. "This administration threw the entire weight of the federal government into prosecuting Davey Hearn, and their actions surrounding his arrest and indictment demand full accountability." In response, a DOJ spokesperson told Newsweek that it, along with the Inspector General, "independently and makes its own decisions about what to review.” A Department of Interior spokesperson said Tuesday that Hearn admitted to officers that he had tampered with the pool, citing court documents detailing reports by National Park Service employees. Newsweek’s reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here. Contact Newsweek editors on this story:John Fitzpatrick and Gray R. Thomas
news.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the Reflecting Pool is 'totally complete' and will be filled up this week.

news.title: US Prosecutors Add Torture Charges Against Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro
news.text:
Edited by: Sean Sinico
US prosecutors have announced new charges against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, accusing them of conspiring to torture political opponents and US citizens.
The new charges against the couple are in addition to the drug-trafficking charges they previously faced, according to a revised indictment released Thursday.
Both Maduro and Flores have denied the previous charges brought against them.
Maduro's lawyer Barry Pollack said in a statement, "President Maduro denies the charges in the new indictment and looks ​forward to his day ‌in court."
Revised indictment adds pressure on Maduro
The revised indictment alleged that the couple committed human rights violations as part of a scheme to hold on to power.
High tensions between the US and a socialist and oil-rich Venezuela were a constant during Maduro's 13 years in power.
Human rights groups have long accused Venezuelan officials of torturing detainees, but Thursday's indictment marks the first time that Maduro could be held to account over the allegations.
"He authorized the use of torture against specific individuals and oversaw a system designed to use torture, arbitrary detention and violence as a means of repression against the political opposition," the indictment said.
The allegations include electric shocks, beatings and asphyxiation at Maduro's behest.
Maduro's wife seeks release from New York jail
Meanwhile, the 69-year-old Flores is due in Manhattan federal court on Thursday. She is expected to ask a judge to release her from jail and place her under house arrest, citing health problems.
Her lawyers say she has lost 25 pounds (11.4 kilograms) in custody, suffers from dizziness and shortness of breath and may have suffered a minor heart attack in July.
They have proposed that she live at a New York residence under 24-hour security.
Prosecutors, however, oppose the request, arguing that Flores poses an "extreme risk of flight and danger to the public” if released.
They said she has received hospital treatment when necessary while in custody.
Trump vs. Maduro
Maduro, 63, and Flores are being held at a federal detention center in Brooklyn as they await their trial in June next year.
The couple was captured during an unprecedented middle-of-the-night raid on their Caracas home on January 3, which was hailed by US President Donald Trump as a "surgical law enforcement operation."
Critics have accused Trump of operating outside international law.
They were subsequently brought to New York, where they face existing drug trafficking and firearms charges.
Maduro has maintained his innocence, calling himself a prisoner of war and referring to his capture as a kidnapping.
Meanwhile, in August, Trump announced that the US had reached a deal to take control of part of Venezuela's vast oil reserves, which Venezuelan Interim President Delcy Rodriguez also termed "historic."
